stem: A held batch looks completely healthy. Who should release the hold?
choices: Any trained technician may release the hold after a documented inspection shows no visible problem.
The worker responsible for the affected space may release it if keeping the hold would disrupt production.
The role authorized by the controlled procedure should make the release decision using the required evidence.
The person who originally placed the hold should release it once the condition they noticed is no longer visible.
rationale: A hold is a controlled status, not simply a visual label. Healthy appearance can be useful evidence, but release authority belongs to the role defined by the facility procedure and may require additional checks or documentation. Technician I should maintain the hold and provide observations rather than releasing it based on convenience or personal judgment.
